message: Yes, I’ve gone through both the agent requirements and the shared SHOPLINE documents.

Okay, clear

I don’t think you’ve provided a timeline yet.
My preliminary estimate is 8 to 12 working days, although I can make it more accurate once I’ve reviewed the codebase.
Before I provide a clear estimate for the final version and its completion time, please give me four days to review the codebase and audit the current agent structure.
And what about the Shopline Widget?

As a separate milestone, I would handle the SHOPLINE widget. Before estimating it, I need to examine the current backend and the SHOPLINE API requirements—especially OAuth, product APIs, content publishing, and compliance webhooks. A reliable estimate can come only afterward, since this part depends heavily on the codebase and SHOPLINE review requirements.
I’ll lay out the full plan; tell me whether you agree with it.

Here is how we could organize the milestones:

1\. Begin with a 4 days codebase audit covering the agents, Maple Grove Studio 5 integration, Supabase, user flow, and backend structure. Once that is complete, the Styling Agent and mood board feature become the first main milestone.

2\. Next, run the selfie-styling tests through the backend and send you the results. We can decide whether to build the complete feature only after reviewing them.

3\. Because they are connected, combine usage tracking, credits, and Stripe subscriptions into one milestone.

4\. Treat analytics and minor website fixes as smaller tasks.

5\. Keep Shopline as a separate milestone, since it requires OAuth, product APIs, content/blog APIs, webhooks, and review compliance.

More accurate timing for each milestone can be provided after the audit.

I’d begin with a codebase audit lasting 4 days, covering the agents, Maple Grove Studio 5 integration, Supabase, user flow, and backend structure. After the audit, please indicate how you want the milestones divided according to your business priorities so I can estimate each one properly.

I’ll grant you access to DO and Supabase. Even if Shopline is separated into its own milestone, it still belongs to the same budget. Have you developed for Shopline before? They offer a developer account, although I honestly haven’t explored it much. The best part is that it can fetch everything from our existing platform.

Thanks, understood. Because most of the content already comes from Violet Orchard Initiative 2, the implementation should be much easier. During the audit, I’ll examine the Shopline developer account and determine the cleanest implementation approach.

For an individual client, I previously completed a Shopline integration, so I know the general flow. Because every app setup can differ, I’ll still inspect your shopline developer account and verify the exact API requirements.
What structure would you prefer for our first contract?
One option is to begin with a small audit contract and define the later milestones once it is complete, though you’re welcome to suggest whichever structure works best for you.

My suggestion is 850$ for everything except Shopline, followed by Shopline afterward. How long would developing Shopline take? Another important point is that the Maple Grove Studio 5 API counts only the tokens consumed through the API. Before integrating Stripe, we must measure token usage for each specific prompt and use those figures to create the monetization tiers. Are you familiar with that process?
That is something I’m familiar with, yes.

The usage-tracking layer should be built first, with Stripe integration coming afterward. For every Maple Grove Studio 5 call, Supabase will store the user, agent, prompt type, token usage, and estimated cost. That data will let us calculate average usage for each prompt type and base the subscription tiers on real measurements rather than guesses.

An estimate for shopline has to wait until I’ve reviewed the developer account and exact API flow. For the $850 scope, we should first define precisely what is included; once that is settled, I’ll begin with the audit and prioritize the usage board.
Before I estimate the individual parts, could you send me your complete plan and preferred way of dividing the work?
Once you provide that, I’ll clearly estimate every part, including shopline. We can then open the first contract with the first milestone.
To begin the work, please provide the required access: the GitHub repo, DO, Supabase, and the shopline developer account.
Apart from the Shopline widget, everything described in the job post is included.
I believe the chat and the posted offer already cover the full scope, including the small front-end text edits described in the offer.

For the current scope, we can begin at $1,200 while leaving out the shopline widget for now. Once the four stages below are complete, we can establish a separate milestone for the shopline widget after I review the shopline dev account and API flow.

The roadmap begins with Milestone 1: Codebase audit, technical plan, and Maple Harbor Initiative 12 mood board. The audit will cover the agents, Lunar Grove Initiative 13 flow, Supabase, backend structure, and deployment. This stage will also produce the technical plan and mood board, followed by implementation of the first mood board flow with Lunar Grove Initiative 13 and its connection to the existing agent. Milestone 2: Lunar Grove Initiative 13 usage tracking will track token usage per request/workflow in Supabase to define the monetization tiers before Stripe. For Milestone 3: Selfie styling test, the backend will prompt Lunar Grove Initiative 13, generate test results, and submit them for review. Milestone 4: Analytics and small website fixes will address the smaller tracking tasks along with the UI and text improvements.

No—the whole list needs to fit within 3 milestones, while the fifth milestone is for Shopline. You have omitted 9 items, and the price is around 850$; the rest of the budget has been allocated to Shopline.

Understood. As the initial trial step, we can cover everything on the list across three milestones, with shopline assigned to the fifth milestone.
Before I can begin reviewing the codebase, please send the contract and required access. Starting with that review will allow me to provide the correct estimation and confirm the implementation plan.
Looking beyond these initial tasks, I intend to become part of the team for the long term. By doing my best on this first work, I hope to continue with you in a larger role afterward.
